The '''Smelter''' is a structure used to process certain raw metals into ingots.

== Building ==
It is be unlocked when the player acquires a {{Item link|Surtling Core}}. It must be constructed near a [[Workbench]].

Smelters can be placed directly onto terrain and stone structures. Currently, they cannot be placed on wood structures, but it is possible to bypass this to an extent by terraforming terrain with a [[Hoe]] to be in line with wooden floors.

== Usage ==
The Smelter is used to process certain raw materials into [[metal]] using {{Item link|Coal}} as fuel. Materials that can be smelted are:

|}
<references group="Note" />

Ingots produced are dropped out in the '''front''' of the smelter, indicated by the angled chute. The smelter also requires free space on the '''left''' to be filled with ore and on the '''right''' to be filled with coal.

The Smelter uses 1 {{Item link|Coal}} every 15 seconds as fuel. It takes 30 seconds<ref><small>Ores used to take 31 seconds to smelt, but this was fixed in [https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/892970/view/3220644827970865344 update 0.208.1].</small></ref> to produce one bar of [[metal]].

It can hold a total of 20 Coal and 10 ores.

== Notes ==
* Like other structures that process materials, smelters are sped up with the passage of time that happens when the player is [[sleeping]].
* When destroyed with a [[Hammer]] or other means, it drops all materials used. It is therefore possible to alternate between using a Smelter and the [[Charcoal Kiln]], reconstructing them as needed.
* Smelters require adequate venting for the smoke above them, otherwise they will stop smelting.
* The smelter, while active, gives off the [[Fire Effect|Fire effect]] for about 4.5 meters from any side (not just the interaction point).
* Advanced metals have to be smelted using a [[Blast Furnace]] instead.

They are the very first biome the player encounters in ''Valheim,'' making them simultaneously the least difficult. Large clearings and sloping hillsides are punctuated by thickets and forests of [[Beech]], [[Birch]], and [[Oak]] trees; underfoot is a carpet of ferns, saplings, and the occasional cluster of [[Raspberries|berry bushes]]. [[Deer]] and wild [[Boar|Boars]] graze peacefully from the grass while diminutive [[Greyling|Greylings]] scurry about, looking for structures and players to damage. Streams and rivers wind and carve their way through the landscape, sometimes opening up to inland seas and lakes, stout [[Neck|Necks]] bathing in the sun along their shores. On the whole, the Meadows make for some of the most pleasant vistas the tenth world has to offer. The biome is not without its hazards, however. '''Viking Graveyards''' are [[Points of interest]] found in the [[Meadows]].

== Description ==
Viking Graveyards appear as stones shaped like a Viking [[Longship]]. Random trees and boulders will spawn within the 'ship' outline, so the Graveyard can be camouflaged somewhat.

A [[Skeleton]] can spawn once in the Viking Graveyards, but only during the night.

==Loot==
Digging around these areas will result in the player discovering a [[Loot chest#Viking Graveyard Chest|Viking Graveyard Chest]] with a 80% chance, two skeletal remains (which give one [[Bone Fragments]] upon pickup), and a 50% for a [[:Category:Valuables|valuable]] among 1-4 [[Amber]], 2-14 [[Coins]] or 1-2 [[Amber Pearl]].

The treasures are buried along the central line of the ship, roughly all at the same depth equivalent to three or four pickaxe hits.
A [[Wishbone]] will lead the player directly to the chest, although the loot is not likely to be worth it for a player at that stage of the game.

'''Troll Caves''' are [[Points of Interest (POI)#Dungeons|dungeons]] found in [[Black Forest|Black Forests]]. 

== Description ==
They appear as large rock formations with a large entryway, usually decorated with two or three bone piles.

Troll caves have a 75% chance to have a [[Troll]] inside, and a 33% chance to have one outside the cave. Trolls do not respawn inside the cave, since they are a single-use [[Spawn points|spawn point]], nor do Trolls in the forest return to a cave. Trolls cannot enter or leave, and nothing other than the player can enter the cave, making an empty troll cave a completely safe refuge.  

It is possible to build a [[campfire]] inside a troll cave without being choked by smoke. The only other structures allowed are a [[Cooking Station]], a [[Sitting Log]], and a [[ward]] (the last of which would be useless, since the cave is classified as a dungeon and [[Workbench|workbenches]] cannot be placed there).

== Loot ==
* [[Amber Pearl]]
*[[Ruby]]
*[[Amber]]
* [[Bone Fragments]]
* [[Coins]]
* [[Yellow Mushroom]]
* Up to two chests. They belong to the same group as the Troll inside the cave, so they only appear if that Troll does (75%). Each chest then has a 75% chance to appear (56.3% overall). Each chest contains:
{{Chest|Troll Cave Chest}}

== Notes ==
* Similar to [[Burial Chambers]], some loot may be spread out across the ground inside the cave, and can be easy to miss.
*A troll cave makes an excellent foundation for an outpost, since no matter how strong the attack, you cannot be reached in any way if you retreat inside the cave, and objects placed in the chests inside the cave are absolutely secure. 
*Unlike other loot, the [[Yellow Mushroom|yellow mushrooms]] in Troll Caves will respawn.

They are the source of {{Item link|Tar}}. == Resources == Tar Pits can be drained by digging a trench from the tar pit to a lower level location (see gallery). Tar nodes can be found in and around Tar Pits. They contain {{Item link|Tar}} and can only be harvested by hand if the Tar Pit is sufficiently drained first. Small nodes yield 4 Tar, big nodes located at the bottom of the pit yield 15 Tar. A single Tar Pit location contains between 69 and 108 Tar. Tar Pit are typically guarded by four or more [[Growth|Growths]]. If they are killed, two Growths respawn in the area after one hour, even if the tar is drained. Destroying bones found around Tar Pit rewards players with {{Item link|Bone Fragments}}. Swimming in a tar pit applies the [[Tarred]] debuff and slows down the player. == Notes == * Tar Pits cannot be set on fire with a [[Torch]] or otherwise. * Any items dropped in Tar Pit become impossible to retrieve until the Tar pit is drained. * Items stuck in tar will not despawn. * Growths are naturally hostile to most other creatures in the Plains as they belong to the undead faction. == Trivia == * Tar pits were introduced in the [[Hearth & Home]] update. == Gallery == File:Tar pond.png File:Growth.png File:Nodes.png|Comparison picture of larger vs. smaller nodes found at the bottom of the pit. '''Frost Caves''' are [[Points of Interest (POI)#Dungeons|dungeons]] found in the [[Mountain]]s.

== Description ==
The entrance is composed of a spiky rock formation with large, blue icicles hanging from the roof of the cave mouth. These caves are the lairs of [[Cultist]]s, [[Ulv]]s, [[Bat]]s, and rarely [[Stone Golem]]s.

Bats lurk in deep shafts down into the mountain. Ulvs may be found in the icy caves or in worked-stone lairs with Cultists. Stone Golems can be found as a rare spawn in deep caves around an icy lake.

Frost Caves may also contain a [[Runestone|vegvisir]] that shows [[Moder]]'s nearest location.

The natural parts of the caves are dimly lit, with patches of light from cracks in the ceiling, or occasional standing torches by chests or altars. Glowing [[crystal]] formations may also be found on the floor and walls of the cave. [[Standing Brazier]]s can be found in the worked-stone portions of the caves and provide heat and light.

A rare feature that can spawn deep in the caves is a large frozen lake, guarded by one to three [[Stone Golem]]s. By the shore of this frozen lake the player can find a runestone left by a weary traveler, the remains of his campfire, and a [[Fishing Rod]] he left behind (which, when looted, also drops two to four [[Fishing Bait]]).

== Strategy ==
Walls of blue ice frequently block passages in the caves and will need to be broken. This can be done with any weapon, pickaxe, or even determined punching. Breaking these walls does create noise that will alert nearby creatures. These walls may not always hide a passage, but sometimes a plain cave wall or a stone with ancient markings. The ice walls have cracks in them that can give a hint to what lies beyond them if a player can peek through.  

One unique feature of Frost Caves are icicles hanging from the ceiling and growing up from the floor. They will break if struck by a powerful enough attack. Weapons will lose durability with these attacks, so swinging wildly may cause a lot more wear and tear on the player's gear. The icicles can be knocked loose from the ceiling, and will drop and do significant damage to anything below them with the same disregard for human life as a falling tree. This is the biggest concern when using [[Stagbreaker]] or an [[Iron Sledge]] in the Frost Caves.

A skilled archer can knock icicles down onto the heads of enemies instead of simply taking the easy route and shooting the enemy. Impaling enemies with falling icicles is challenging, but gratifying.

Another environmental peril of Frost Caves is the uncaring force of gravity. The caves frequently feature vertical shafts that may or may not have precarious paths down into them. Falling down one of these shafts will, of course, hurt. [[Bat]]s often spawn in these vertical shafts and in the chaos of their rapid fly-bys a careless character can find themselves baited by these flying creatures into a quick trip to the bottom. The good news is that if a player falls down into a hole that has no path up, there will be a way up from the bottom, just not the way they arrived. These shafts can be cleared with a running jump or sometimes have narrow ledges that will allow a cautious explorer to move by. 

The lairs of the [[Cultist]]s are behind wooden doors ([[Wood]] and sometimes [[Iron]] when destroyed), and feature a wide range of breakable objects, from furniture for [[Finewood]], to bones for [[Bone Fragments]], to tapestries of matted hair for [[Fenris Hair]]. The [[Red Jute]] curtains obscure vision, often hiding enemies. One strategy is to use an [[Iron Sledge]] to simply demolish everything, but this will obviously alert any inhabitants. These lairs may contain altars with Fenris hair and [[Fenris Claw]]s and Cultists, as well as rooms and corridors that can contain [[Ulv]]s. If Ulvs are detected, [[Ooze Bomb]]s are useful, since werewolves are vulnerable to poison. The tight corridors and poor sight-lines often make combat up close and personal, but a stealthy player may be able to use a bow in some areas. 

These lairs also feature piles of meat which have standard drop of [[Entrails]] with a chance to drop extra [[Coins]], [[Silver Necklace]] and [[Entrails]]. Altar rooms are the most rewarding, as they can have 0-4 jute and hair tapestries, with 0–5 additional knots of hair hanging beneath each one. The altar may have 2 or 4 offerings of Claws or hair, but they are guarded with 0–3 Cultists.

The '''Standing Brazier''' is a light source that can be placed on any surface, and must be built within the range of a [[Forge]].

==Usage==
The Standing Brazier has all the same functions as a [[Campfire]] and is a [[Player base|base]] structure.

Standing Braziers are fueled with [[Coal]]. With 1/5 fuel, a Standing Brazier will last for 5 hours and 33 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Standing Brazier should burn for 27 hours and 47 minutes. It can be used for cooking, however, it does not fit easily like a [[Campfire]] does.

The [[Fire Effect]] for the Standing Brazier extends for about 4–5 meters (Measured from the closest the player can stand without setting themselves on fire).

==Notes==
* Destroying the Standing Brazier with a [[Hammer]] will not yield back any [[Coal]] and will only return the 5 [[Bronze]] and 3 [[Fenris Claw]]s used for its construction. All Coal used as fuel and for the initial construction will <u>not</u> be dropped.
* Standing Braziers found in [[Frost Caves]] can be destroyed for Coal and sometimes Bronze.
* Standing Braziers stop working if exposed to rainy weather without a roof.

== Usage ==
The '''Shield generator''' dome protects the player and structures within:
* Protects from [[Rain]], prevents players from getting the [[Wet Effect]] and structures from being damaged. (Similar to the [[Shelter Effect]])
* Protects from [[Cinder rain]] in [[Ashlands]], prevents the structure from catching on fire from falling cinder.
* Protects against incoming projectiles such as [[Creatures]] attacks.
* Protects against [[Lava]] balls randomly coming from lava lakes, useful when mining [[Flametal Ore Vein]]s close to lava edge.

== Behavior ==
The Shield generator can be built upon solid ground, [[Cage Structures|Cage]], [[Stone Structures|Stone]], [[Black Marble Structures|Black marble]] or [[Grausten Structures|Grausten]] structures.

The radius of effect is 30 meters in a spherical area centered on the Shield generator.

The generator can hold up to 10 [[Bone Fragments]] or [[Charred Bone]] as fuel and consumes one fuel per 500 damage. Damage will occur when a projectile with an origin outside the radius of effect comes into contact with the shield edge, absorbing the projectile in the process. These absorbed projectiles include the environmental Cinders, and any combat projectiles, ranged or magical, produced by players or creatures. Although the effects of Rain are nullified by the shield, this effect will not cause damage, or consume fuel of the shield generator.

The radius of two or more shields overlapping will result in their intersection combining, allowing multiple shields to be chained together into a larger shield.

== Trivia ==
* Due to the shield determining whether to block an incoming projectile based on its origin position, it is possible for the player to fire a projectile from within the shielded region, and as it exits and re-enters the region, will not be absorbed by the shield.
* Though the effects of Rain are nullified, the Shield generator will not protect [[Fire Effect]] yielding structures from being extinguished, still requiring Shelter.

== Tips ==
* The Shield generator is useful for [[Farming (Skill)|Farming]], where most crops must not be placed under Shelter, normally forcing the player to farm under the effects of rain.

6000 (gates) | tool tier = 5 |resources = * [[Loot chest#Charred Fortress Charred Chests|Charred chest]] * [[Bell Fragment]] * [[Molten Core]] | resistances = pickaxe only | number = 20 }} '''Charred Fortresses''' are [[Points of interest]] in [[Ashlands]]. They are marked by a beam of green light shooting straight up into the sky, visible from a distance. == Location == Each world has 20 Charred Fortresses. They are always located away from the coasts between the inland lava fields, usually inside the central islands of the Ashlands. == Layout == The fortress consists of a tall, rectangular outer wall with many pillars and spiked bronze defenses. Two opposing outer walls have closed gates in them, leading to the interior area. The interior contains an expanse of ground littered with gravestones, with two [[Effigy of Malice|Effigies of Malice]] in the corners and two stone ramps leading up to the parapets atop the exterior walls. In the very center of the fortress interior is a tall tower, capped with more spiked defenses, which has one gate leading inside. The walls (of the exterior and of the interior tower), the pillars, gates and spiked defenses can all be destroyed, but only by [[Damage#Pickaxe|Pickaxe damage of tool tier 5 or higher]] - i.e. a [[Battering Ram]] or a [[Catapult]] with [[Explosive Payload]]s. The pillars have negligible (1) health but the walls (1500), spikes (1500) and especially the gates (6000) have much higher health. The exterior walls are three layers thick, whereas the interior tower walls are only one layer thick. The fortress initially spawns some creatures, independently to the Effigies of Malice, they do not respawn if killed: * Up to 3 [[Charred Warlock]]s (100% chance for the one on top of the tower and 60% chance to spawn for the other). * Up to 5 [[Charred Marksman|Charred Marksmen]] (100% chance for the one on top of the tower and 60% chance to spawn for the other). * Up to 4 [[Skugg]]s (80% chance for each corner of the fortress to have one). == Loot == Inside the central tower can be found: * A Bell Altar, drops 2 to 4 {{Item link|Bell Fragment}}s when destroyed. * A [[Loot chest#Charred Fortress Charred Chests|Charred chest]]. * A [[Vegvisir|Fader Vegvisir]] with a 50% chance to spawn. * 2 [[Molten Core]]s. Other places inside the Fortress: * The interior court can have up to 8 [[Molten Core]]s, with a 5% chance each to spawn. * Up to 3 Charred chests can spawn along the solid walls of the tower (clockwise from the tower entrance: 100%, 13% and 50% chances to spawn). * [[Skugg]] drop {{item link|Charred Cogwheel}}s which allow the player to make a [[Catapult]]. * The bronze spike strips can be destroyed to drop 2-5 [[Scrap Bronze]] each. As each Charred Fortress contains exactly 78 spike strips, one fortress will yield an average of 273 scrap bronze. The content of Charred Chests is: {{Chest|Charred Chest}} == Notes == * The exterior walls (3 layers x 1500 health = 4500 total) are easier to break through than the gates (6000 health). The tower walls (1500 health) are easier still, but be careful not to accidentally destroy any loot (see below). * The Charred chests and the Bell fragment altar are destroyable; while the chests have 200 health and are resistant to most types of damage (except for [[Damage#Lightning|Lightning]], [[Damage#Poison|Poison]] and [[Damage#Spirit|Spirit]]), the altar is extremely fragile - having only 10 health and no damage resistances. * The presence of the Bell fragment altar is indicated by a huge vertical beacon of light, which can be seen at a distance. This beacon can help identify the location of intact fortresses from afar. ** Destroying the altar also removes the beacon. * The eastern and western smaller islands usually generate with no fortress, thus it is best to first land directly south of spawn. * Some segments of the walls can be mined with any pickaxe. This might be due to a bug. == Tips == * A simple strategy to conquer Charred Fortresses is to first master one Charred Fortress, obtain a [[Bloodstone]], and then craft the [[Trollstav]]. Now, the player can easily approach a Charred Fortress and summon [[Summoned Troll]]s from the outside, which will handle the fortress without any issues. Finally, kill the Troll and enjoy the loot! * It is easier to build a wooden ladder to get on top of the wall rather than using a [[Battering Ram]] to destroy the gates/walls. And, if you are lucky with the world generation, you could use one of the naturally spawning giant rocks to get inside too. Once on top of the walls, simply run circles in the walls and slowly kill enemies and destroy the [[Effigy of Malice|spawners]], if you get overwhelmed just jump off outside (be careful if there is lava). * You can destroy the [[Skugg|skuggs]] from outside the fortress with the bow/crossbow or magic, and from a high enough place you can also destroy the [[Effigy of Malice|spawners]] too. * If you conquered the fortress and didn´t destroy the walls/gates to get inside, the fortress is now a perfect place to build a mini base, thanks to the indestructible walls. Only the flying [[Fallen Valkyrie|valkyries]] and [[Volture|Voltures]] can get inside. * There are two ways to get inside the central tower without a [[Battering Ram]]. First is to make a hole on the ground with a pickaxe and simply pass below the wall of the tower (this may not work if you hit the limit on how low the ground can go). Second is to get on top of the tower and get inside through the hole between the spikes, to get out you will need to either portal out or build yourself ladders/platforms to pass through the hole between the spikes again. == Gallery == Charred fortress tower interior.png|The inside of a Charred Fortress tower. '''Frost Foundry''' is a structure used to craft in the [[Deep North]]. It hardens [[Moulds|Casts]] into finished Deep North weapons, armor, shields, staffs and the {{Item link|Intricate Key}}.

==Building==
The Frost Foundry is found in the Crafting category of the [[Hammer]] and requires a nearby [[Workbench]] to build. It cannot be placed in water or on sloped surfaces. It costs:
* {{Item link|Iron|15}}
* {{Item link|Stone|20}}

A [[Moulds|Cast]] can be placed at the center to create the final item. The Frost Foundry holds one cast at a time. The process consumes five Liquid Frost and takes 50 seconds. Finished items cannot burn if left inside. Items made in the Frost Foundry come out at full durability.
